review.notes: Machine-drafted by an AI model; awaiting review by a Latinist. House style: simple Church Latin, spelled without macrons, with u/v and i/j as in Stage 0 (v and i only); present tense, with a few perfects (venit, vidit, fuit, dixit) in the last units.

english.source: drafted with the text; not reviewed

sentences.text: Hodie hospes in urbe est. Hospes ex urbe Roma venit.
sentences.english: Today a guest is in the town. The guest comes from the city of Rome.

sentences.text: Hospes ad domum Marthae it. Martha in porta est.
sentences.english: The guest goes to Martha's house. Martha is at the door.

sentences.text: Salve! Estne haec domus Marthae?
sentences.english: Hello! Is this Martha's house?
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Salve! Martha sum. Haec domus mea est. Quis es tu?
sentences.english: Hello! I am Martha. This is my house. Who are you?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Hospes sum. Nomen mihi Paulus est. Ex urbe Roma venio.
sentences.english: I am a guest. My name is Paul. I come from the city of Rome.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Salve, Paule! Veni in domum!
sentences.english: Hello, Paul! Come into the house!
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Gratias tibi ago, Martha. Urbs Roma longe est, et fessus sum.
sentences.english: Thank you, Martha. The city of Rome is far away, and I am tired.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Sede, Paule! Aquam bibis? Lac bibis?
sentences.english: Sit, Paul! Do you drink water? Do you drink milk?
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Aquam volo. Gratias tibi ago.
sentences.english: I want water. Thank you.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Ecce aqua. Panem quoque habes. Panis bonus est.
sentences.english: Here is water. You have bread too. The bread is good.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Panem libenter edo. Tu bona es, Martha.
sentences.english: I gladly eat bread. You are good, Martha.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Samuel et Marcus in domum veniunt. Hospitem vident.
sentences.english: Samuel and Marcus come into the house. They see the guest.

sentences.text: Salve! Quis est ille, Martha?
sentences.english: Hello! Who is that, Martha?
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Ille hospes est. Nomen ei Paulus est. Ex urbe Roma venit.
sentences.english: He is a guest. His name is Paul. He comes from the city of Rome.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Salve, hospes! Nomen mihi Marcus est. Puer sum.
sentences.english: Hello, guest! My name is Marcus. I am a boy.
sentences.speaker: nico

sentences.text: Salve, Marce! Et quis est ille?
sentences.english: Hello, Marcus! And who is that?
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Samuel sum. Hic in urbe habito.
sentences.english: I am Samuel. I live here in the town.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Tu quoque hospes es?
sentences.english: Are you a guest too?
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Hospes sum, sed hic habito. Amicos bonos habeo.
sentences.english: I am a guest, but I live here. I have good friends.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Ubi est ecclesia? Cras ad ecclesiam eo, quia dies Dominica est.
sentences.english: Where is the church? Tomorrow I go to church, because it is Sunday.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Ecclesia non longe est. Ibi Deum laudamus. Cras ad ecclesiam imus.
sentences.english: The church is not far. There we praise God. Tomorrow we go to church.
sentences.speaker: marta

sentences.text: Libenter ad ecclesiam eo. Gratias tibi ago, Martha.
sentences.english: I gladly go to church. Thank you, Martha.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Hospes in domo Marthae manet. Marcus quoque in domo manet. Martha panem et lac habet, et hospes bene edit.
sentences.english: The guest stays in Martha's house. Marcus stays in the house too. Martha has bread and milk, and the guest eats well.

sentences.text: Post cenam hospes dicit: In urbe nova amicos bonos habeo. Deus bonus est.
sentences.english: After supper the guest says: In the new town I have good friends. God is good.

sentences.text: Martha dicit: Deo gratias! Pax tibi, Paule.
sentences.english: Martha says: Thanks be to God! Peace to you, Paul.

sentences.text: Hospes epistulam habet. Epistula ex urbe Roma est. Mater Samuelis epistulam scribit.
sentences.english: The guest has a letter. The letter is from the city of Rome. Samuel's mother writes a letter.

sentences.text: Samuel, ecce epistula! Mater tua epistulam scribit, et ego epistulam habeo.
sentences.english: Samuel, look, a letter! Your mother writes a letter, and I have the letter.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Epistula! Gratias tibi ago, Paule. Mater mea bona est. Pater quoque epistulam amat.
sentences.english: A letter! Thank you, Paul. My mother is good. My father loves the letter too.
sentences.speaker: sam

sentences.text: Mater tua dicit: Pax tibi, Samuel. Deus tecum est.
sentences.english: Your mother says: Peace to you, Samuel. God is with you.
sentences.speaker: hospes

sentences.text: Deo gratias! Libenter epistulam audio. Hodie dies bonus est.
sentences.english: Thanks be to God! I gladly hear the letter. Today is a good day.
sentences.speaker: sam
